thread:
Mira: Heads-up — I want to follow up on the SLO-aware rate / quota refactor we sketched in the RFC a few months ago. Thinking about ownership and the runtime contract.
Sam: Nice — did you mean the part where the admission controller exposes per-tenant soft-SLO feedback?
Mira: Yep. We hit a few production surprises last week; need to tighten the interface.
Diego: Can you summarize the surprises?
Mira: Two things: 1) when a tenant spikes we try soft-shed but downstream model variants don't get a clear callout, so they keep warm GPUs -> cost spikes. 2) our old probe tokens for fairness didn't carry SLO priority metadata, so ingress routing sometimes routes high-cost bursts to cheaper but higher-latency capacity.
Annah: Oof. So we need an explicit SLO signal in the admission API and a clear side-channel for rollback/fallback hints.
Sam: Agreed. Proposal: admission response includes {decision, admitted_tokens, slo_label, hint_set}. hint_set can be small enums like [DEGRADE_MODEL, FALLBACK_REGION, REDUCE_BATCH].
Mira: Sketch config block I sent earlier looked like this:```yaml
admit_response:
  decision: ADMIT | SOFT_SHEd | REJECT
  admitted_tokens: 120
  slo_label: "p95-200ms"
  hints:
    - DEGRADE_MODEL
```
Diego: That looks good. Need to be careful with enums — downstream runtimes must not assume a hint is always actionable. Hints are suggestions, not commands.
Sam: Right. Also we should add a capability field in the admission request so runtimes can advertise what they can do: e.g., supports_model_degrade: true, supports_region_fallback: false. That way admission can choose hints it knows will be consumed.
Mira: Good call. So new contract: Request includes runtime_capabilities map, response includes slo_label + hints.
Annah: How will this affect metrics and billing? We need to record when a hint is acted on vs ignored.
Diego: Add boolean flags to the admission ack telemetry: hint_accepted: true/false and hint_type. Emit sample rate to reduce cardinality.
Sam: Also we should add a bounded schema version header so older runtimes ignore unknown fields. header: X-Admission-Schema: v1.1
Mira: Migration plan idea: 1) rollout schema header support (backwards compatible) 2) publish enum list and capability names 3) start emitting hints as opt-in via feature flag 4) flip default after 2 weeks of opt-in telemetry.
Annah: Who owns the publish and the enum registry? eng-platform or runtime?
Mira: Registry lives in eng-platform (single source of truth), but runtime teams own capability flags and act on hints.
Diego: Ops-bot: can we gate rollout by region? We should test in us-west first, then eu.
ops-bot: noted — can create canary rollout: eng-platform feature-flag 'slo-hints' scoped to us-west and 10% of traffic.
Sam: Edge case: what if hints suggest DEGRADE_MODEL but the customer pinned a model version? Admission should honor customer pins and instead return FALLBACK_REGION or REDUCE_BATCH.
Mira: Add rule precedence: customer_pin > tenant_slo_protection_policy > runtime_capability. That way pins win.
Annah: We should also update Console (redwood console) to show hint counts and hint-accepted ratio per-tenant. Product wants a new column for "hint-utilization".
Diego: Implementation tasks: a) admission proto change, b) runtime capability adder, c) telemetry update, d) console UX cell, e) docs and migration playbook.
Sam: I'll own the proto and server changes. Diego, can you coordinate the runtime changes?
Diego: Yup, will create RFC PR with compatibility tests.
Mira: I'll draft a short follow-up RFC that captures the contract + migration + ownership. Target: 2-week sync, rollout after ops canary.
Annah: One more: rate-limit fairness — we need to ensure the new SLO-aware admission doesn't starve low-priority long-running jobs. Add a soft-fairness token bucket with a drain-rate floor.
Sam: Let's add that as a separate subticket; it'll need simulation with current traffic traces.
Mira: Cool. Action items recorded. I'll post the RFC draft in #eng-platform tomorrow and tag folks. :raised_hands:
